title: In This Town — Who Bit the Town?
logline: In this town, every morning one house wakes up with a giant bite taken out of it. The town paints everything green to stay safe and nobody touches the string on top of the clock tower. Unpaid detective me follows the clues (the bites taste sweet, there are sprinkles on the street, the bite mark has a tooth missing), then sets a hot-sauce trap on our bubblegum-pink roof and catches the biter: a giant gap-toothed kid. He wasn't eating the town. He was checking if it was ready.
twist: Every clue was a cake clue. The walls taste sweet, the sprinkles are sprinkles, nothing bites green because kids hate veggies, and the silver wall at the edge of town is the rim of a plate. Our town is the giant kid's birthday cake, the party is tomorrow, and the string on top of the clock tower nobody is allowed to touch is a candle wick. Last shot: a gigantic match strikes in the sky.
caption_hook: Something takes one bite out of our town every night. The clues were there the whole time.
sets: Narrator's pink house roof (dusk flashback, night)
Aerial plate shot: the whole town sitting on a giant silver plate against a dark void

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: In this town, every morning, one house wakes up with a giant bite taken out of it.
beats.visual: Sunrise (day preset, warm). Slow push-in down Main Street to a pink house with a huge stepped half-circle bite missing from its roof corner, crumb cubes on the lawn. A crowd of extras stares; the narrator (me) in front, surprised pose, shocked face. Far behind, the shiny silver rim at the edge of town glints (plant).

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: First the bakery. Then the post office. Then Mrs. Plum's garage.
beats.visual: Three whip-pan cuts: the bakery with its roof bitten; the post office with its chimney bitten off; Mrs. Plum (old lady, purple hair, glasses) standing in her garage, which is cut clean in half, crossArms, sweat face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Nobody has seen who. We just hear one giant crunch at three in the morning.
beats.visual: Quiet night preset. Wide shot of Main Street, every window dark, the clock tower face at 3:00. A hard camera shake, then one window light pops on.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: So, two rules. One: paint your house green. Nothing ever bites green.
beats.visual: Day. Montage of extras with big paint rollers turning houses bright green; one untouched green house stands next to two bitten pastel ones.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Two: never touch the string on the clock tower. Nobody knows why.
beats.visual: Low-angle tilt up the clock tower to a thick black string sticking straight up from its roof (the wick, planted). Two townspeople glance up at it and shrug.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Mr. Bramble painted his house green. And his cat. And himself.
beats.visual: Mr. Bramble (mustache, totally green: skin, clothes, everything) stands proudly in front of his green house, crossArms, smug face; a green-tinted cat sits at his feet.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: My mom refused. Our house stays bubblegum pink, because it's a vibe.
beats.visual: The narrator's bubblegum-pink house with mint trim. Mom (sunglasses) lounges in a lawn chair out front and shrugs; the narrator facepalm-shrugs beside her.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: So I'm investigating. Detective. Unpaid.
beats.visual: Kid's bedroom. The narrator in a detective cap over his headphones, at his desk in front of a corkboard of house photos and red string, think pose, smug face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: First clue: the bites taste sweet. Don't ask how I know.
beats.visual: Close-up: the narrator leans in and licks the edge of a bitten pink wall, then snaps back with a shocked face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Second clue: rainbow sprinkles all over the street.
beats.visual: Low camera skims the road at sunrise, which is covered in tiny rainbow sprinkles; the narrator crouches with a magnifying glass, peer pose.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Third clue: the bite has a gap. The biter's missing a front tooth.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of the bite edge: a scalloped row of tooth notches with one big square gap. A red circle pops around the gap.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: Bedroom. The narrator slams his fist into his palm (slam pose), huss face, a hard punch-in on each HUSS; the corkboard shakes and a photo drops.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Everyone blamed Big Gus. But Gus has all his teeth.
beats.visual: Town square. A crowd of extras points at Big Gus (huge guy, beard, cap) holding a tall pancake stack. Gus grins wide and shows a full, perfect row of teeth.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: So I made a trap. If it likes sweet, let's see how it likes spicy.
beats.visual: Me (MAIN.me) on the bubblegum-pink roof at dusk with a paint roller, painting the roof bright red with a giant bottle of GRANDMA'S EXTRA SPICY hot sauce beside me, a smug determined face. Flames-icon stamp.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Then last night, the crunch was on my street.
beats.visual: Quiet night, the narrator's bedroom. The room shakes (camera shake), a giant shadow slides across the window, the narrator sits bolt upright in bed, shocked face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: A giant fork stabbed down and lifted our roof off like a cracker. Then it bit.
beats.visual: Night, storm-dark sky. An enormous silver fork (long box handle, four box tines) stabs down out of the clouds into our pink house, lifts the red hot-sauce roof off like a cracker and carries it up; a giant CRUNCH. Camera shake.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Then the fork came back for me.
beats.visual: The fork swoops down at me standing in my roofless bedroom; I dive aside.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Ah, almost... almost!
beats.visual: Freeze-frame: the giant fingertips an inch from the narrator's hood, him mid-dive with a sweat face. Record scratch, big stamped word.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Then the sky yelled...
beats.visual: The fingers jerk back up into the clouds. The whole night sky flashes red; camera shake.

beats.speaker: giantkid
beats.text: Spicy!
beats.visual: A gigantic blocky kid head rises over the rooftops behind the clock tower, red cheeks, tongue out, eyes squeezed shut, fanning his mouth with a giant hand. Delivered in a separate deep, booming giant-kid voice.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The narrator stands on the roofless pink house pointing up, huss face. Lights flick on house by house down the street and townspeople pour out pointing; a camera shake on each HUSS.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: A giant kid. Missing a front tooth.
beats.visual: Low-angle hero shot: the giant kid peeks sheepishly over the rooftops and grins, showing a big gap where a front tooth should be.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: He wasn't eating our town. Just checking if it was ready.
beats.visual: A giant hand gently sets the red roof back on the pink house. The giant kid's face is sheepish and sweaty; the narrator watches with crossArms.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Ready for what?
beats.visual: Close-up of the narrator: shrug pose, squint face.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Then I noticed the silver rim around town. Like a plate.
beats.visual: The camera cranes up and up above the town until we see all of it sitting on a giant round silver plate with a shiny rim. Pastel houses look like frosting decorations and sprinkles cover everything.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: Our town isn't a town. It's his birthday cake.
beats.visual: Top-down shot: the giant kid, now wearing a party hat, leans over the plate-town grinning his gap-tooth grin.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: And nothing bites green? No kid eats the vegetables.
beats.visual: Top-down crane over the town: the green-painted houses sit like leftover broccoli garnish on a giant cake; Mr. Bramble (painted green) waves up.

beats.speaker: me
beats.text: HUSS! HUSS! HUSS!
beats.visual: The narrator on his roof, stunned pose into huss face, with a punch-in on each HUSS; behind him the giant kid tries to copy the HUSS with his mouth wide open.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: His party's tomorrow. And that string on the clock tower? It's a candle wick.
beats.visual: Close-up on the black string on top of the clock tower. Above it a gigantic match strikes in the night sky, flares into a glowing flame cone and slowly lowers toward the wick, lighting the whole town orange.

beats.speaker: narr
beats.text: And somebody just struck a match.
beats.visual: Low angle from the street up past the clock tower: in the dark sky a gigantic match strikes with a burst of orange light, and the flame lowers toward the string (wick) on top of the clock tower. Hard cut to black.
